Theme 043 · Metaphor concepts

The Weather Forecast

Your product's health becomes a weather map. A Doppler scope sweeps over sectors named after your metrics, range rings count the minutes until customers would feel it, and one storm cell blooms over Checkout. A human forecaster makes the call, and the film ends in clear skies.

readability ●●○trust ●●○effort med
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Fog drifts right across a TV five-day card while the days flip in left to right, one per beat. Friday's card turns coral with a lightning bolt on the last downbeat and the red ticker slides in from the left: the warning came too late.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

The TV card collapses into a dot that becomes the scope centre; range rings ripple outward. On the drop the beam makes its first clockwise pass and "Acme Pulse" lights in its wake.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

The beam sweeps clockwise (3.2 s per turn); cells ignite as it passes and fade behind it. In the Checkout sector a cell turns amber, then coral, on the downbeat of bar 2; the dashed ring locks on, the datablock types in and the forecaster taps "Roll back".

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The storm shrinks and desaturates, the scope brightens into a morning sky and the sun rises from the lower right. The tagline lands on the downbeat; the "FRI · CLEAR" strip slides up from the bottom on the final bar.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Five-day card — TV-weather strip that stages the hook (fog all week, storm on Friday).
  • Radar scope — range rings as minutes until customers would feel it; sectors named after metrics.
  • Conic sweep — single gradient beam with a fading trailing edge; the agent's heartbeat.
  • Storm cell — teal→amber→coral blurred blobs; only one ever reaches coral.
  • Datablock — mono readout tethered to the cell with the anomaly text.
  • Forecaster bar + outlook strip — the human decision, then "FRI · CLEAR" in the CTA.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Sweep — @property angle 0→360° over 3.2 s, linear; that is 6.4 beats at 120 BPM, so start each turn on a bar line and let it phase across the loop.
  • Cell ignition — each cell's delay = its angle ÷ 360 × 3.2 s so it lights exactly as the beam hits; fades 95%→12% over 1.5 s.
  • Storm clears — resolved cells shrink and desaturate in a 0.08 s stagger, power2.in, starting on the downbeat after "Roll back".

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Everyone reads weather maps instantly, and "forecast" frames the product as early warning rather than post-mortem. Risk: storms read as bad news, and a busy scope is hard at 1:1; resolve fast, cap it at five sectors and end in sunshine.

Adapt to your product: Name the sectors after your own signals (queues, regions, customers, cost) and let the rings mean whatever "time until it hurts" is for you.
